**Fill in the blank with the correct verb form:**

Scarcely had the CEO concluded her speech when the shareholders _____ to their feet.
solution:
The correct answer is '**rose**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The verb "**rose**" is the simple past tense form of the verb "**rise**."
 
• The sentence describes an action that occurred immediately after another past event ("**Scarcely had the CEO concluded her speech**"), so the past tense "**rose**" is required.
 
• **Options 2, 3**, and 4 are grammatically incorrect in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"Scarcely had the CEO concluded her speech when the shareholders **rose**__ to their feet."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "had risen"** is incorrect because it implies a past perfect tense, which is unnecessary in this context.
 
• **Option 3: "had rose"** is incorrect as it is grammatically incorrect; the correct past participle of "rise" is "risen."
 
• **Option 4: "were risen"** is incorrect because this construction is not used in standard English for this context.
